chapters.title: Superior to the Angels
chapters.html:
Hebrews 1

God Has Spoken in His Son

1Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets,

2but in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom also He made the ages.

3He is the radiance of His glory and the exact imprint of His being, and He upholds all things by His powerful word. After making purification for sins through Himself, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,

4having become as much superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is more excellent than theirs.

The Son Above the Angels

5For to which of the angels did God ever say,
"You are My Son;
today I have fathered You"?
Or again,
"I will be His Father,
and He shall be My Son"?

6Again, when He brings the firstborn into the world, He says,
"Let all God's angels worship Him."

7Of the angels He says,
"He makes His angels winds,
and His servants a flame of fire."

8But of the Son He says,
"Your throne, O God, is forever and ever,
and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of Your kingdom.

9You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness;
therefore God, Your God, has anointed You
with the oil of gladness above Your companions."

10He also says,
"You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning,
and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

11They will perish, but You remain;
they will all wear out like a garment;

12like a robe You will roll them up,
like a garment they will be changed.
But You are the same,
and Your years will have no end."

13To which of the angels has He ever said,
"Sit at My right hand
until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet"?

14Are they not all ministering spirits sent out to serve those who are to inherit salvation?

Notes

  • v3 "the radiance of His glory" — apaugasma, the word the Wisdom of Solomon uses of Wisdom: she is a reflection of eternal light (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26, apaugasma). What Wisdom was said to be, the Son is.

  • vv6–7 "Let all God's angels worship Him… He makes His angels winds" — both lines are in the Greek Bible and not in the Hebrew. The first is not word for word in either: the Greek of Moses' song has let the sons of God worship Him and, two lines on, all the angels of God (Deuteronomy 32:43), where the Hebrew has only Rejoice, nations, with His people; the Greek of Psalm 97:7 has worship Him, all His angels, where the Hebrew has all gods. The second is Psalm 104:4, He makes the winds His messengers in the Hebrew; the Greek has angels and spirits, pneumata, which is winds as well. The writer builds his argument on the Greek.

chapters.title: Made Like His Brothers
chapters.html:
Hebrews 2

Do Not Drift Away

1For this reason we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away from it.

2For if the message spoken through angels proved firm, and every transgression and disobedience received its just penalty,

3how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was first spoken by the Lord, and it was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,

4while God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various mighty works and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.

The Son Made Lower for a Little While

5For it was not to angels that God subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking.

6But someone has testified somewhere,
"What is man, that You remember him,
or the son of man, that You visit him?

7You made him for a little while lower than the angels;
You crowned him with glory and honor,

8putting all things under his feet."
In putting everything under him, He left nothing outside his control. At present, we do not yet see everything under him.

9But we see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that apart from God He might taste death for everyone.

10For it was fitting that He, for whom and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the founder of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

11For He who makes holy and those who are made holy all have one origin. That is why He is not ashamed to call them brothers,

12saying,
"I will tell of Your name to My brothers;
among the congregation I will sing Your praise."

13Again,
"I will put My trust in Him."
Again,
"Here am I and the children God has given Me."

14Since therefore the children share in blood and flesh, He Himself likewise shared in the same things, so that through death He might destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil,

15and set free all those who through fear of death were held in slavery all their lives.

16For surely it is not angels that He helps, but He helps the seed of Abraham.

17Therefore He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.

18For because He Himself has suffered when tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.

Notes

  • vv6–9 "You made him for a little while lower than the angels" — Psalm 8:4–6 in the Greek. The Hebrew has You have made him little less than God, me'at me-Elohim; the Greek has brachy ti par' angelous, which can mean a little lower or for a little while lower. The psalm speaks of humankind; the writer reads it of Jesus, who was lower for a little while and is now crowned with glory and honor.

  • v9 "apart from God" — chōris theou, the reading of the Greek edition (SBLGNT), which marks the place as one where manuscripts differ; the other reading is chariti theou, by the grace of God. Apart from God can mean that He tasted death for all things except God, or that He tasted it forsaken, as He cried, My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me? (Mark 15:34).

chapters.title: Today, If You Hear His Voice
chapters.html:
Hebrews 3

Jesus Greater Than Moses

1Therefore, holy brothers, who share in a heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession,

2who was faithful to Him who appointed Him, just as Moses also was faithful in God's house.

3For Jesus has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, as much as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself.

4For every house is built by someone, but the builder of all things is God.

5Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant, to testify to the things that were to be spoken later,

6but Christ is faithful over God's house as a Son. We are His house, if we hold fast our confidence and our boasting in our hope.

Do Not Harden Your Hearts

7So, as the Holy Spirit says,
"Today, if you hear His voice,

8do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion,
on the day of testing in the wilderness,

9where your fathers put Me to the test
and saw My works for forty years.

10Therefore I was disgusted with this generation,
and I said, 'Their hearts always go astray;
they have not known My ways.'

11So I swore in My anger,
'They shall not enter My rest.'"

12Take care, brothers, that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.

13But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called "Today," so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

14For we have come to share in Christ, if indeed we hold our first confidence firm to the end.

15As it is said,
"Today, if you hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion."

16For who were those who heard and rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt led by Moses?

17With whom was He disgusted for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

18To whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, but to those who disobeyed?

19So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.

Notes

  • vv7–11 "as in the rebellion, on the day of testing" — Psalm 95:7–11 in the Greek, which turns the Hebrew's place names into what they mean: where the Hebrew has as at Meribah, as on the day of Massah, the Greek has in the rebellion, parapikrasmos, and of testing, peirasmos. The names come from the rock at Horeb, where the people quarreled and tested the LORD (Exodus 17:7).

chapters.title: A Sabbath Rest
chapters.html:
Hebrews 4

The Rest That Remains

1So, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us fear that any of you should seem to have fallen short of it.

2For we have had the good news proclaimed to us just as they did; but the message they heard did them no good, because they were not united in faith with those who listened.

3For we who have believed enter that rest, as He has said,
"So I swore in My anger,
'They shall not enter My rest,'"
although His works were finished from the foundation of the world.

4For somewhere He has spoken of the seventh day in this way: "God rested on the seventh day from all His works."

5Again, in this passage: "They shall not enter My rest."

6Since therefore it remains for some to enter it, and those who formerly had the good news proclaimed to them did not enter because of disobedience,

7He again sets a certain day, "Today," saying through David so long afterward, in the words already quoted,
"Today, if you hear His voice,
do not harden your hearts."

8For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken of another day later on.

9So then, there remains a sabbath rest for the people of God,

10for whoever has entered God's rest has also rested from his works, as God did from His.

11Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, so that no one may fall by the same kind of disobedience.

The Living Word

12For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

13No creature is hidden from His sight, but all are naked and laid bare to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.

Our Great High Priest

14Since then we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession.

15For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tested in every way as we are, yet without sin.

16Let us then draw near with confidence to the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

Notes

  • vv3–10 "My rest… God rested on the seventh day… a sabbath rest" — the argument turns on one Greek word. Psalm 95 says They shall not enter My rest, katapausis, and the Greek of Genesis 2:2 says God rested, katepausen, on the seventh day. The Hebrew of Genesis has He ceased, shavat, the root of sabbath, and v9 names what is left for God's people with a word found nowhere else, sabbatismos, a sabbath rest.

  • v8 "if Joshua had given them rest" — Iēsous, the Greek of the name Joshua and the name of Jesus. Joshua brought the people into the land, but the psalm, written long after, still says Today: the rest was not yet given.

chapters.title: A Priest Like Melchizedek
chapters.html:
Hebrews 5

1For every high priest chosen from among men is appointed to act on behalf of men in relation to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

2He can deal gently with the ignorant and the wayward, since he himself is beset with weakness.

3Because of this he is obliged to offer sacrifice for his own sins just as he does for those of the people.

4No one takes this honor for himself, but only when called by God, just as Aaron was.

5So also Christ did not exalt Himself to be made a high priest, but was appointed by Him who said to Him,
"You are My Son;
today I have fathered You";

6as He says also in another place,
"You are a priest forever,
after the order of Melchizedek."

7In the days of His flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and pleas, with loud cries and tears, to Him who was able to save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

8Although He was a Son, He learned obedience through what He suffered.

9Having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him,

10being designated by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

Milk and Solid Food

11About this we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, since you have become slow to hear.

12For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you again the first principles of God's words. You need milk, not solid food,

13for everyone who lives on milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, since he is a child.

14But solid food is for the mature, for those whose senses have been trained by practice to tell good from evil.

as He says also in another place, "You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek."

being designated by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

chapters.title: An Anchor of the Soul
chapters.html:
Hebrews 6

Go On to Maturity

1So let us leave the elementary teaching about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,

2of instruction about washings, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

3This we will do, if God permits.

4For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and have shared in the Holy Spirit,

5and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come,

6and then have fallen away, to restore them again to repentance, since they are crucifying the Son of God once again for themselves and holding Him up to contempt.

7For land that drinks the rain that often falls on it, and produces a crop useful to those for whose sake it is farmed, receives a blessing from God.

8But if it bears thorns and thistles, it is worthless and near to being cursed, and its end is to be burned.

9But in your case, beloved, we are convinced of better things, things that belong to salvation, even though we speak in this way.

10For God is not unjust so as to forget your work and the love you have shown for His name in serving the saints, as you still do.

11We want each of you to show the same eagerness to have the full assurance of hope until the end,

12so that you may not be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

The Sure Promise of God

13For when God made a promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater by whom to swear, He swore by Himself,

14saying, "I will surely bless you and multiply you."

15So Abraham, having patiently waited, obtained the promise.

16For people swear by something greater than themselves, and an oath confirms what is said and puts an end to all argument.

17So when God wanted to show more convincingly to the heirs of the promise that His purpose could not change, He guaranteed it with an oath,

18so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us.

19We have this hope as an anchor of the soul, sure and steadfast, a hope that enters into the inner place behind the curtain,

20where Jesus has gone in ahead of us on our behalf, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

chapters.title: Melchizedek
chapters.html:
Hebrews 7

The King of Righteousness

1For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the defeat of the kings and blessed him,

2and Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. His name means first king of righteousness, and then he is also king of Salem, that is, king of peace.

3He is without father or mother or genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God he remains a priest forever.

4See how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils!

5Those descendants of Levi who receive the priesthood have a command in the Law to take tithes from the people, that is, from their brothers, though these also are descended from Abraham.

6But this man, who does not share their descent, received tithes from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.

7It is beyond dispute that the lesser is blessed by the greater.

8In the one case tithes are received by men who die, but in the other by one of whom it is testified that he lives.

9One might even say that Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham,

10for he was still in the loins of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.

A Priest of a Different Order

11Now if perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood (for on the basis of it the people received the Law), what further need would there have been for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, rather than one named after the order of Aaron?

12For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.

13For the one of whom these things are said belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.

14For it is plain that our Lord came from Judah, and in connection with that tribe Moses said nothing about priests.

15This becomes even more plain when another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,

16who has become a priest not on the basis of a legal requirement about bodily descent, but by the power of an indestructible life.

17For it is testified of Him,
"You are a priest forever,
after the order of Melchizedek."

18On the one hand, a former commandment is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness

19(for the Law made nothing perfect); on the other hand, a better hope is brought in, through which we draw near to God.

20It was not without an oath. Those men became priests without an oath,

21but this one was made a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him,
"The Lord has sworn
and will not change His mind:
'You are a priest forever.'"

22By so much Jesus has become the guarantor of a better covenant.

23The former priests were many in number, because they were prevented by death from continuing in office,

24but He holds His priesthood permanently, because He continues forever.

25So He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

26For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

27He has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for their own sins and then for those of the people; He did this once for all when He offered up Himself.

28For the Law appoints men in their weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the Law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "king of Salem… without father or mother or genealogy" — the whole of Melchizedek's story in Genesis is three verses (Genesis 14:18–20), and they give no father, no birth and no death. The writer reads the silence: a priest whose beginning and end are not recorded stands for the priest who remains forever, as Psalm 110:4 says, You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek. His name and his city carry righteousness (tsedeq) and peace (shalom).

See how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils!
Those descendants of Levi who receive the priesthood have a command in the Law to take tithes from the people, that is, from their brothers, though these also are descended from Abraham.
But this man, who does not share their descent, received tithes from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.
It is beyond dispute that the lesser is blessed by the greater.
In the one case tithes are received by men who die, but in the other by one of whom it is testified that he lives.
One might even say that Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham,
for he was still in the loins of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.
A Priest of a Different Order

Now if perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood (for on the basis of it the people received the Law), what further need would there have been for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, rather than one named after the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
For the one of whom these things are said belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
For it is plain that our Lord came from Judah, and in connection with that tribe Moses said nothing about priests.
This becomes even more plain when another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
who has become a priest not on the basis of a legal requirement about bodily descent, but by the power of an indestructible life.
For it is testified of Him, "You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek."
On the one hand, a former commandment is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness
(for the Law made nothing perfect); on the other hand, a better hope is brought in, through which we draw near to God.
It was not without an oath. Those men became priests without an oath,
but this one was made a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him, "The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: 'You are a priest forever.'"
By so much Jesus has become the guarantor of a better covenant.
The former priests were many in number, because they were prevented by death from continuing in office,
but He holds His priesthood permanently, because He continues forever.
So He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.
For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
He has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for their own sins and then for those of the people; He did this once for all when He offered up Himself.
For the Law appoints men in their weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came after the Law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.html:
Hebrews 8

The Minister of the True Tent

1Now the main point of what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,

2a minister in the holy places and in the true tent, which the Lord set up, not man.

3For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, so it is necessary for this one also to have something to offer.

4If He were on earth, He would not be a priest at all, since there are those who offer the gifts according to law.

5They serve at a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was instructed when he was about to finish the tent: "See," He says, "that you make everything by the pattern that was shown you on the mountain."

6But as it is, He has obtained a ministry as much more excellent as the covenant He mediates is better, a covenant enacted on better promises.

The First Covenant Made Old

7For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no place sought for a second.

8For He finds fault with them when He says:
"Days are coming, says the Lord,
when I will establish a new covenant
with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

9not like the covenant that I made with their fathers
on the day I took them by the hand
to bring them out of the land of Egypt;
for they did not continue in My covenant,
and I turned away from them, says the Lord.

10For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel
after those days, says the Lord:
I will put My laws into their minds,
and on their hearts I will write them;
and I will be their God,
and they will be My people.

11No one will teach his fellow citizen
or his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,'
for they will all know Me,
from the least of them to the greatest.

12For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoing,
and I will remember their sins no more."

13When He says new, He has made the first one old; and what is becoming old and growing aged is near to vanishing.

Notes

  • v5 "by the pattern that was shown you on the mountain" — Exodus 25:40, See, and make them by their pattern, which you are being shown on the mountain, in the Greek kata ton typon, by the pattern. Hebrews reads it as the LORD's own word that the tent Moses built was made after something he was shown, so the earthly tent is a copy and shadow; in 9:24 the holy places made with hands are antitypa, copies, of the true ones. Stephen quotes the same command of the tent of witness (Acts 7:44).

  • v9 "they did not continue in My covenant, and I turned away from them" — Jeremiah 31:32 in the Greek (38:32 there), ēmelēsa autōn, I turned away from them, or I disregarded them. The Hebrew reads My covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, ba'alti bam. Hebrews quotes the Greek throughout vv8–12, and its I will put My laws into their minds and I will be merciful toward their wrongdoing are the Greek's words as well.

chapters.title: The Blood of the Covenant
chapters.html:
Hebrews 9

The Earthly Tent

1Now even the first covenant had regulations for worship and a sanctuary of this world.

2For a tent was prepared, the first one, in which were the lampstand and the table and the bread of the Presence; it is called the Holy Place.

3Behind the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,

4which had a golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant, covered on all sides with gold. In the ark were a golden jar holding the manna, and Aaron's staff that budded, and the tablets of the covenant.

5Above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the atonement cover. Of these things we cannot now speak in detail.

6With these things prepared in this way, the priests go continually into the first tent to carry out their services,

7but into the second only the high priest goes, once a year, and not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins the people have committed unknowingly.

8By this the Holy Spirit makes plain that the way into the holy places has not yet been revealed while the first tent is still standing.

9This is a figure for the present time. Under it, gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot make the worshiper perfect in conscience,

10since they deal only with food and drink and various washings, regulations for the flesh imposed until the time of setting things right.

The Blood of Christ

11But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, through the greater and more perfect tent not made with hands, that is, not of this creation,

12He entered once for all into the holy places, not by the blood of goats and calves, but by His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.

13For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who have been defiled, make them holy for the cleansing of the flesh,

14how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without defect to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!

15That is why He is the mediator of a new covenant: since a death has taken place to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant, those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.

16For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established.

17A will takes effect only at death; it never has force while the one who made it is alive.

18So not even the first covenant was put into effect without blood.

19When every commandment of the Law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of the calves, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

20saying, "This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you."

21In the same way he sprinkled with the blood both the tent and all the vessels used in worship.

22Under the Law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

Once for All

23So it was necessary for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

24For Christ did not enter holy places made with hands, copies of the true ones, but heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf.

25Nor was it to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the holy places year by year with blood not his own,

26for then He would have had to suffer again and again since the foundation of the world. But as it is, He has appeared once, at the end of the ages, to put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

27Just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after that comes judgment,

28so Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but for the salvation of those who are eagerly waiting for Him.

Notes

  • v4 "a golden altar of incense" — chrysoun thymiatērion. In the Greek Old Testament the word is used only for a censer: Uzziah's in the temple (2 Chronicles 26:19), the elders' in Ezekiel's vision (Ezekiel 8:11). The golden altar of incense of Exodus stood before the curtain, thysiastērion thymiamatos there (Exodus 30:1, 6). So the verse can mean the altar, the one golden object of incense the tent had, set with the inner room it served, or a golden censer kept inside it.

  • vv16–17 "where there is a will" — diathēkē, the word that is covenant in v15 and v18. In everyday Greek it was a person's will, which takes effect only when its maker dies. The writer moves from one sense to the other without a new word: the new covenant is also an inheritance (v15), and it came into force by a death. Read as covenant throughout, vv16–17 speak of the death of the victim by which a covenant was ratified, the blood of v18.

  • v20 "This is the blood of the covenant" — Exodus 24:8, Here is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has cut with you. Hebrews has touto, this is, the words of Jesus at the supper: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many (Mark 14:24).

  • v28 "offered once to bear the sins of many" — Isaiah 53:12, yet he carried the sin of many, in the Greek hamartias pollōn anēnegken, the verb and words Hebrews uses.

chapters.title: One Sacrifice for All Time
chapters.html:
Hebrews 10

A Body You Prepared for Me

1For since the Law has only a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very form of the realities, it can never, by the same sacrifices offered continually year after year, make perfect those who draw near.

2Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered? The worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have any consciousness of sins.

3But in these sacrifices there is a reminder of sins year after year,

4for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

5That is why, when He comes into the world, He says:
"Sacrifice and offering You did not desire,
but a body You prepared for Me;

6in burnt offerings and sin offerings
You took no pleasure.

7Then I said, 'Here I have come —
in the scroll of the book it is written of Me —
to do Your will, O God.'"

8When He said above, "Sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You take pleasure in them" (these are offered according to law),

9then He said, "Here I have come to do Your will." He takes away the first in order to establish the second.

10By that will we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

11Every priest stands day after day serving and offering again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.

12But this one, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,

13waiting from then on until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.

14For by one offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being made holy.

15The Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,

16"This is the covenant that I will make with them
after those days, says the Lord:
I will put My laws on their hearts,
and on their minds I will write them,"

17He adds,
"I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more."

18Where these have been forgiven, there is no longer any offering for sin.

Let Us Draw Near

19So, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,

20by the new and living way that He opened for us through the curtain, that is, through His flesh,

21and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

22let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

23Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for He who promised is faithful.

24Let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works,

25not neglecting to meet together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.

A Fearful Expectation

26For if we go on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,

27but a fearful expectation of judgment, and a fury of fire that will consume the adversaries.

28Anyone who has set aside the Law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

29How much worse punishment, do you think, will be deserved by the one who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, and has treated as common the blood of the covenant by which he was made holy, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

30For we know Him who said, "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay." Again, "The Lord will judge His people."

31It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

Do Not Throw Away Your Confidence

32But remember the former days, when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings,

33sometimes being made a public spectacle by insults and afflictions, and sometimes becoming partners with those who were treated so.

34For you shared the sufferings of the prisoners, and you joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you yourselves have a better possession, one that lasts.

35So do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward.

36For you need endurance, so that when you have done the will of God you may receive what was promised.

37"For yet a very little while,
and the One who is coming will come and will not delay;

38but My righteous one will live by faith,
and if he shrinks back,
My soul has no pleasure in him."

39But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and keep their souls.

Notes

  • v5 "but a body You prepared for Me" — Psalm 40:6 in the Greek (39:7 there), sōma de katērtisō moi. The Hebrew reads ears You have dug for me, oznayim karita li: an ear opened to hear and obey. Hebrews quotes the Greek, and builds on its word in v10: through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. In both witnesses the psalm sets God's will above sacrifice; the Greek names the body that does it.

  • vv37–38 "the One who is coming… My righteous one will live by faith" — Habakkuk 2:3–4 in the Greek, opened with mikron hoson hoson, a very little while, from Isaiah 26:20. Habakkuk's Greek says of the vision, coming it will come; Hebrews adds the article, ho erchomenos, the One who is coming. It puts the Greek's two lines in the other order, so that the one who shrinks back is the righteous one himself, and it reads My righteous one, where Habakkuk's Greek has by My faith and the Hebrew by his faithfulness. Paul quotes the same line without My (Romans 1:17; Galatians 3:11).

chapters.title: By Faith
chapters.html:
Hebrews 11

What Faith Is

1Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen.

2For by it the people of old received God's approval.

3By faith we understand that the ages were put in order by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that appear.

From Abel to Abraham

4By faith Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain, and through it he was approved as righteous, God bearing witness over his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks.

5By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken up he was approved as having pleased God.

6Without faith it is impossible to please Him, for whoever draws near to God must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who seek Him.

7By faith Noah, when he was warned by God about things not yet seen, in reverent fear built an ark to save his household. Through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.

8By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.

9By faith he lived as a guest in the land of promise, as in a foreign land, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.

10For he was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God.

11By faith, with Sarah herself, he received power to father a child, even past the age for it, since he considered Him faithful who had promised.

12So from one man, and him as good as dead, were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as countless as the sand by the shore of the sea.

Seeking a Homeland

13These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.

14For people who speak this way make it plain that they are seeking a homeland.

15If they had been thinking of the country they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.

16But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. That is why God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.

From Abraham to Moses

17By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac; he who had received the promises was offering up his only son,

18of whom it was said, "Through Isaac your seed shall be called."

19He reckoned that God was able even to raise him from the dead; and from there, in a figure, he did receive him back.

20By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.

21By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and bowed in worship over the top of his staff.

22By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.

23By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's edict.

24By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,

25choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin,

26considering the reproach of the Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking to the reward.

27By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king, for he endured as seeing Him who is invisible.

28By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.

The Rest of the Witnesses

29By faith they crossed the Red Sea as on dry land, but the Egyptians, when they attempted it, were swallowed up.

30By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after they had been encircled for seven days.

31By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had welcomed the spies in peace.

32What more shall I say? Time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,

33who through faith conquered kingdoms, carried out justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,

34quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.

35Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing to accept release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.

36Others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and prison.

37They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed with the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, mistreated,

38people of whom the world was not worthy, wandering in deserts and mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.

39All these, though approved through their faith, did not receive what was promised,

40since God had foreseen something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect apart from us.

Notes

  • v1 "the assurance of things hoped for" — hypostasis, literally what stands under. This book has used it twice already: of God's own being, of which the Son is the exact imprint (1:3), and of the confidence we hold firm to the end (3:14). So faith may be the assurance of things hoped for, held in the believer, or their substance, the reality they already have before they are seen.

  • v5 "he was approved as having pleased God" — Genesis 5:24 in the Greek, Enoch pleased God, and he was not found, because God took him. The Hebrew reads Enoch walked with God. He was not, for God took him. Hebrews quotes the Greek words and builds v6 on them: without faith it is impossible to please Him.

  • v11 "with Sarah herself, he received power to father a child" — autē Sarra, as the edition prints it, with Sarah herself; the same words without the mark of the dative are Sarah herself. Dynamin eis katabolēn spermatos, power for laying down seed, is said of a father, and the sentence goes on: from one man, and him as good as dead (v12). So Abraham receives power, with Sarah. Read with Sarah as the subject, the verse is the faith of the barren wife (Genesis 11:30) who laughed at the promise (Genesis 18:12).

  • v21 "bowed in worship over the top of his staff" — Genesis 47:31 in the Greek, at the top of his staff. The Hebrew reads at the head of the bed. The two words are written with the same letters, mittah, bed, and matteh, staff; the Greek read the second.

speech.text: Hebrews 11
What Faith Is
Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen.
For by it the people of old received God's approval.
By faith we understand that the ages were put in order by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that appear.
From Abel to Abraham
By faith Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain, and through it he was approved as righteous, God bearing witness over his gifts; and through it, though he died, he still speaks.
By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken up he was approved as having pleased God.
Without faith it is impossible to please Him, for whoever draws near to God must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who seek Him.

By faith Noah, when he was warned by God about things not yet seen, in reverent fear built an ark to save his household. Through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a guest in the land of promise, as in a foreign land, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.
For he was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose designer and builder is God.
By faith, with Sarah herself, he received power to father a child, even past the age for it, since he considered Him faithful who had promised.
So from one man, and him as good as dead, were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as countless as the sand by the shore of the sea.
Seeking a Homeland
These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.
For people who speak this way make it plain that they are seeking a homeland.
If they had been thinking of the country they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.
But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. That is why God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.
From Abraham to Moses
By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac; he who had received the promises was offering up his only son,
of whom it was said, "Through Isaac your seed shall be called."
He reckoned that God was able even to raise him from the dead; and from there, in a figure, he did receive him back.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and bowed in worship over the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's edict.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing rather to be mistreated with the people of God than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin,
considering the reproach of the Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking to the reward.
By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king, for he endured as seeing Him who is invisible.
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
The Rest of the Witnesses
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as on dry land, but the Egyptians, when they attempted it, were swallowed up.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after they had been encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had welcomed the spies in peace.
What more shall I say? Time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, carried out justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.
Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing to accept release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
Others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and prison.
They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed with the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, mistreated,
people of whom the world was not worthy, wandering in deserts and mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.
All these, though approved through their faith, did not receive what was promised,
since God had foreseen something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect apart from us.
